title: First ALMA observations of the HD 105211 debris disc: A warm dust component close to a gigayear-old star
question: What is the structure (radius, width, eccentricity, asymmetry) of the HD 105211 debris disc at ALMA 1.3 mm, and is there a warm dust component near the star?

data.arrays: 12m array (44 antennas in OB1, 45 in OB2)
data.angular_resolution: combined-image beam 1.62'' x 1.57'' (32 au x 31 au), PA 40.2 deg; OB1 beam 2.25 x 1.85 arcsec, OB2 beam 1.41 x 1.11 arcsec

what.value: SED photometry from optical to millimetre (Table 2, references numbered 1-13 in the table)

evidence.quote: we collected observational data from literature papers, including photometric measurements from optical to millimetre wavelengths

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the 1.3 mm continuum
recipe.method: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA, 10 s time averaging, tclean continuum imaging with natural weighting

recipe.goal: Measure surface brightness profiles and ansa asymmetry
recipe.method: Radial profiles along major and minor axes with radial averaging in 10 deg-wide swaths; compare peak fluxes of the two ansae
key_parameters: SW ansa peak 158 +/- 16 uJy/beam, about 2 sigma above the opposite ansa

recipe.goal: Image the two observation blocks separately and measure central flux
recipe.method: Individual OB1 and OB2 images; OB2 smoothed to OB1 beam with UV tapering; peak pixel near the stellar position taken as central emission

recipe.goal: Fit parametric disc models to the ALMA visibilities
recipe.method: Axisymmetric Gaussian ring and eccentric ring models, Fourier transformed and sampled at the observed uv points, chi2 against the visibilities; stellar-position point-source flux F_c added
key_parameters: data averaged to 10 s and four channels per spectral window, weights recomputed with statwt
100 walkers, 1000 steps, first 900 discarded as burn-in
assumptions: optically thin torus; uniform posterior distribution functions for all parameters

recipe.goal: Fit OB1 and OB2 separately to test variability and asymmetry
recipe.method: Same Gaussian and eccentric models fitted to each observation block

recipe.goal: Fit the SED with a two-temperature model
recipe.method: PHOENIX stellar photosphere plus modified blackbody disc components; ALMA 1.3 mm flux taken from the visibility fit; warm component forced to near pure blackbody to match the ALMA central flux
key_parameters: modified blackbody: lambda0 = 380 um, beta = 2.3 (cold); lambda0 = 160 um, beta ~ 0 (warm)
assumptions: blackbody multiplied by (lambda0/lambda)^beta for lambda >= lambda0

recipe.goal: Derive disc mass loss, dust mass and radius ratio
recipe.method: Mass-loss rate from steady-state collisional cascade equation; mm dust mass from Wyatt 2008 eq. 5 with kappa = 2.3 cm^2/g; Gamma = actual radius / blackbody radius

recipe.goal: Constrain the warm inner dust component
recipe.method: Compare the observed warm fractional luminosity with the maximum steady-state collisional value at the blackbody radius, and compare the blackbody-like spectrum with cascade expectations
assumptions: two origin scenarios considered: in situ planetesimal belt or comet delivery

recipe.goal: Compare ALMA model with Herschel 70 um profile
recipe.method: Best-fit ALMA model radial profile convolved with the ALMA and Herschel 70 um beams, compared with the Herschel 70 um image profile
